caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 65 of 2001
lawyer:
Mr. Khandakar Mahbub Hossain, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record -----for the petitioner. 
Ms. Seema Zahur, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Firoz Shah, Advocate-on-Record -----for respondent No. 2. 
Respondent No. 1: Not represented
parties:
Ajit Kumar Shaha
Vs.
The State and another
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Amin Chowdhury, CJ : This petition for leave to appeal is against judgment and order dated 29.11.2000 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5138 of 2000 filed for quashing the proceeding of C.R. Case No. 220 of 2000 now pending in the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Narayanganj. 

 2. The short fact leading to this petition is that respondent No. 2 as complainant filed a petition of complaint before the Magistrate, First Class, Narayanganj which is C.R. Case No. 220 of 2000 alleging that the complainant is a Lawyer and house tutor of witness No. 1 and on 20.12.1999 witness No. 1 was waiting for her parents for going to school for appearing in the primary school scholarship examination of 1999 and at that time accused Tazul Islam appeared there and disclosing his identity wanted to know the name of witness No. 1 and told that on 19.12.1999 he will guard witness No. l's hall and he will also do the same on the following day 20.12.1999. It is also the case of the prosecution that witness No. 1 submitted her answer script and after coming out of the hall reported to her parents that she has taken five extra sheets but due to shortge of time she failed to put her roll number and signature in the last sheet. Then the examinee, complainant and his wife went to the Hall Supervisor and wanted to correct the mistake. The Hall in-charge and one Assistant Teacher found out the answer script but without those lose five sheets and it was found that someone has taken away those lose sheets and when the complainant raised objection the hall in-charge requested the complainant to compromise the matter. It is the further case of the prosecution that accused Tazul Islam committed the offence so that witness No. 1 may not get talent poll scholarship which may go to another school at Ramnagar. Subsequently after inquiry cognizance was taken by the Magistrate on 25.6.2000 under sections 477/166 of the Penal Code. Thereafter the accused petitioner moved the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of criminal Procedure for quashing the proceeding but on hearing both the sides the Rule was discharged by judgment dated 29.11.2000. 

 4. We have gone through the judgment of the High Court Division and it appears that the case is at the initial stage and the High Court Division after writing out a detail judgment came to the finding that there is no ground for quashing the entire proceeding. But the proceeding under section 166 of the Penal Code has been quashed. In such circumstances at this stage we refrain ourselves from making comment whether the answer scrip is a valuable security or not as this will be decided by the trial court and the answer script may be a valuable security in a proper case which is to be dealt with by the trial court. We hold that the High Court Division has not committed any illegality and wrong in passing the impugned order. There is therefore, no merit in this petition and the same is accordingly dismissed.
